items.evidence: audio_harness.require_sounds() (tools/audio_harness.py:35-37) exits unless .local/horizon-client/26.2/assets/minecraft/sounds.json exists. The prepared .local (prepare run in progress the morning of 2026-11-24, started 02:49 UTC) has a full assets/minecraft/ tree but no sounds.json and no sounds/ directory; the file is also absent from the client jar (ships only in the asset index). The absence does not depend on the prepare run's completion: sounds are never imported by the --prepare flow. Root cause is prepare: sounds need the separate 'horizon-prepare sounds' subcommand (horizon-prepare/src/main.rs:240) or --complete. Runtime: SoundRegistry::load silently skips a missing sounds.json (sound_events.rs:280-282), so every event resolves to Sound::empty(). Blocks all 6 audio_harness drivers (sound_event, ambient_sound, music, situational_music, sound_engine, audio_attributes); 3 are oracle-clean (sound_event, music, situational_music — data-only block) and 3 are oracle-blocked as well (ambient_sound, sound_engine, audio_attributes — see B10-O04). The wiring spec itself is clean (1,968 sounds.json events vs 1,968 registry events; only the intentionally_empty sentinel lacks an entry, plus one vanilla orphan: entity.chicken_picky.step in sounds.json with no registry event).
items.title: No sounds.json in the prepared 26.2 resources: the game is silent and 6 audio drivers cannot run

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.2 registers 26 BE renderers (BlockEntityRenderers, javap -c); the port's Kind (block_entity_render.rs:321-371) covers 17 slots plus beacon beams, and classify() falls through to Kind::None for the rest. Missing with visible effect: mob/trial spawner spinning mob (+ trial items) — cage is a block model (cube_all_inner_faces / cube_bottom_top_inner_faces), the mob is BE-rendered; campfire cooking items (logs are template_campfire, 7 elements; items BE-rendered); moving piston — moving_piston's block model is EMPTY, PistonHeadRenderer draws the moving block, so it vanishes mid-stroke (port has only collision shapes, collisions.rs:579); brushable-block brushed item (block renders via cube_all sand models); vault display item (template_vault block renders; item BE-rendered); shelf displayed items — NEW for 26.2, ShelfRenderer registered, template_shelf_body renders the shelf but the 3 displayed items are BE-rendered and the port has only the BE data (chunk/block_entity.rs:96-97). Structure-block and test-instance-block renderers are also absent but their visible in-play output is unverified (both have cube block models) — noted, not claimed. potent_sulfur has no vanilla renderer, so rendering nothing for it is correct.
items.title: Seven vanilla block-entity renderers have no port equivalent (spawner, trial spawner, campfire, moving piston, brushable, vault, shelf)

items.evidence: REINSTATED on coordinator reconciliation: the batch agent withdrew this on the import-level check (both font packages exist in 26.2), but the measured Batch 0 table shows a 1-symbol failure. ParityFont.java:43 calls pack.asResourceManager() on a VanillaPackResources; the method does not exist in 26.2 (error: cannot find symbol, symbol: method asResourceManager(), location: variable pack of type VanillaPackResources). Client cp: 1 error; server cp: 41 errors (blaze3d.font is client-only, expected). Repair: find 26.2's way to get a ResourceManager from a VanillaPackResources (javap the 26.2 class). Highest-leverage single-symbol repair in the batch: ParityFont blocks 8 drivers programme-wide (7 in this batch: block_entity_render, chat_screen, hud, pack_screen, recipe_book_render, subtitle, text_display_render) and cascades into VanillaSubtitleOracle and VanillaChatScreenOracle.

items.evidence: VanillaBlockEntityRenderOracle imports net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.UvMapping (line 23), a 26.3-only class absent from the 26.2 client jar (verified against the full 10,952-class list); it casts the SubmitNodeCollector proxy's args[7] to UvMapping at line 155. Measured: 7 errors on the client cp (first error line 23, the import). Blocks test_block_entity_render_parity — the driver that would catch B10-G04. Repair is small: in 26.2, OrderedSubmitNodeCollector.submitModel's 8th parameter IS the TextureAtlasSprite directly (javap), so cast args[7] to TextureAtlasSprite and drop the import; light/overlay/tint positions (args 4/5/6) already match. Note the driver is blocked by two more oracles as well: ParityFont (B10-O02, 1 error) and VanillaTextDisplayRenderOracle (missing-symbol, 1 error); all three must compile before the driver runs. ParityData compiles clean.

items.evidence: com.mojang.renderpearl.* appears ZERO times in the 26.2 client jar — the render-pipeline API the 26.3-derived oracles use does not exist in 26.2. Five oracles import it: VanillaHudOracle (9 errors), VanillaPackScreenOracle (7), VanillaRecipeBookScreenOracle (4), VanillaLoomScreenOracle (4) (each missing renderpearl.api.pipeline.RenderPipeline only) and VanillaWorldBorderRenderOracle (28 errors: GpuBuffer, CommandEncoder, RenderPass, GpuDevice, RenderPipeline, plus net.minecraft.client.renderer.DynamicGpuData). Drivers blocked: hud, pack_screen, recipe_book_render, screen_layout, world_border_render, plus chat_screen (compiles VanillaPackScreenOracle as a dependency, test_chat_screen_parity.py:146). Repair is a 26.3-to-26.2 backport: 26.2 screens render through the SubmitNodeCollector/RenderType path, not a GPU pipeline object. The family's other members, measured: VanillaContainerScreenOracle and VanillaOptionsOracle PASS on the client cp; VanillaChatScreenOracle is a cascade failure (depends on broken ParityFont + VanillaPackScreenOracle); VanillaMenuOracle fails on its own 1 error (3-arg Player.drop with net.minecraft.util.Prediction, absent in 26.2).

systemic_note: Two systemic patterns, both different from 1.21.7. (1) The 26.2 port inherits 26.3's answers, and for Batch 10 they are mostly RIGHT: signs, beds, the swap ticker, the options category chain and the font packages all work for 26.2 because 26.2 IS 26.x — 5 of 1.21.7's 11 defects evaporate. What remains is the genuinely unported residue: the seven BE-rendered extras (spawner mob, campfire items, moving piston, brushable item, vault item, shelf items) that no version's port has drawn, and the 26.3-only APIs (renderpearl, UvMapping, DynamicGpuData, asResourceManager, ClockInstance) that the oracles assumed. (2) The sound stack is blocked on data AND oracles: the morning's prepare ran the export flow only, so the prepared 26.2 resources have no sounds.json — one 'horizon-prepare sounds' run fixes the silent game and unblocks the 3 oracle-clean audio drivers, but ambient_sound, sound_engine and audio_attributes also need their oracles repaired (B10-O04). The wiring spec itself is clean (1,968/1,968 real events, plus one vanilla orphan: entity.chicken_picky.step exists in sounds.json with no registry event). (3) Method lesson: an import-level oracle check is NOT a substitute for the Batch 0 measurement — it missed 12 driver-blocking failures here, all method-level.
